summary: Dependency-confusion lure resolves install-scripted tarball from third-party host
details: kepler@99.99.99 is published with the classic dependency-confusion shape: a suspicious high version number (99.99.99), placeholder author/description metadata, and a package.json that declares a dependency (`flag-serial-object-syntax`) resolved via a direct URL to a non-registry third-party host, https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax. The shrinkwrap pins that URL with hasInstallScript: true, so `npm install` downloads the tarball from artifacts.yosiroute.com and executes its lifecycle scripts on the installer's machine. Kepler itself carries no code of substance; its only install-time effect is to force resolution and execution of code hosted on an attacker-controlled domain outside the npm registry. The 99.99.99 version is designed to win version resolution against a legitimate internal package of the same name in mixed public/private registry configurations.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
